extracted.intended_audience: newcomers to MetaPost / TeX users (students) working on UNIX
extracted.subtask_description: A hands-on introduction to writing MetaPost source files to produce high-quality PostScript/LaTeX graphics: syntax, primitives, macros, styles, and workflows (mpost → .1 → preview/pdf → include in LaTeX).

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming and program invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to end each METAPOST program in a file with extension mp so that this part of the name can be omitted when invoking METAPOST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give source files a .mp extension; invoke with `mpost example` (no extension). METAPOST creates output files like example.1 and example.log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document structure: beginfig/endfig and end
rubrics_metrics.description: A METAPOST document normally contains a sequence of beginfig and endfig pairs with an end statement after the last one. The numeric argument to beginfig determines the name of the output file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrap graphic commands between beginfig(n); ... endfig; and finish the file with end;. The content between a given beginfig/endfig is written to the corresponding example.n output file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement termination and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each statement in a METAPOST program is ended by a semicolon; only in cases where the statement has a clear endpoint (e.g., end and endfig) you may omit superfluous semicolons. You can put two or more statements on one line as long as separated by semicolons. You may also stretch a statement across several lines and insert spaces for readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add comments with %, keep semicolons to avoid parsing errors; prefer explicit semicolons for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating and previewing output (workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: METAPOST converts source .mp into PostScript output (example.1); preview with `gs example.1` or `ggv`; convert to PDF with `epstopdf example.1` and view with Acrobat (`acroread example.pdf`).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware gs may not use the picture bounding box; use ggv or convert to PDF for reliable viewing/printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including MetaPost output in LaTeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the graphicx package and DeclareGraphicsRule to treat .1/.mps files as Encapsulated PostScript for inclusion in LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: use \usepackage{graphicx} and \DeclareGraphicsRule{*}{mps}{*}{} then \includegraphics{example.1}; typeset with `pdflatex sample` to generate sample.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units of length and custom units
rubrics_metrics.description: Default unit is a PostScript point (bp) = 1/72 inch. Other units include in, cm, mm; 1cm is shorthand for 1*cm. You may define your own unit variable, e.g., u = 0.5cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit units for portability and clarity; 0 may be used instead of 0cm. Defining u makes scaling drawings easy (u := 1cm;).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric type and fixed-point limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric quantities in METAPOST are represented in fixed point arithmetic as integer multiples of 2^(-16) and with absolute value less or equal to 4096 = 2^12. METAPOST does not understand exponential notation (e.g., 1.23E4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid very large or extremely small values; use integer arithmetic or break expressions if limits are approached. Use show to inspect numeric values. `warningcheck := 0;` can alter warning behavior during testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default types and explicit declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The numeric data type is the default type of any non-declared variable. Use pair for points/vectors; pair variables are often assigned with `=` whereas numeric uses `:=`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare pair p; then p := (0,0) or p = (0,0). Use xpart P and ypart P to access coordinates. Be explicit about types to avoid accidental numeric/pair confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming conventions that imply subvariables
rubrics_metrics.description: Using names like z0 = (1,2) implies x0 and y0 variables exist and are set. Using dotted names like z.P implies x.P and y.P exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these naming patterns to conveniently bind component variables; be mindful of namespace collisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using `whatever` for parametric/unbound points
rubrics_metrics.description: `whatever[z1,z2]` denotes some point on the line connecting z1 and z2; `whatever` allows specifying a general point without introducing a new named variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use `whatever` to express intersections or parametric positions succinctly, e.g., to find intersection of medians or define a point on a line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connecting points: straight vs. curved segments and closing paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `--` between points to draw straight lines and `..` to draw smooth cubic Bézier curves. Use `cycle` to truly close a path; simply appending the start point only visually closes it but may not make it a closed path for fill operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use `cycle` when you intend to fill interiors (fill requires a really closed path). Choose `--` vs `..` depending on desired geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curve control: automatic control points, tension, curl, and manual controls
rubrics_metrics.description: METAPOST automatically computes cubic Bézier control points so segments have same direction at interior knots. You can manually specify incoming/outgoing directions (up/down/left/right, dir(angle)) or explicit control points with `controls (c0) and (c1)`. `tension` affects curvature; `curl` affects approach at endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust `tension` and `curl` to shape curves; provide explicit control points when precise behavior is required; use `precontrol`/`postcontrol` to inspect generated controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special path operators `...` and `---` meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: The operators are defined in terms of curl and tension: `...` means 'choose an inflection-free path between the points unless endpoint directions make this impossible' (tension atleast 1); `---` means 'get a smooth connection between a straight line and the rest of the curve' (tension infinity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use `...` for natural smooth curves; use `---` when mixing straight segments smoothly with curves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction and angle utilities: dir and angle
rubrics_metrics.description: `dir(theta)` generates a unit circle pair at given angle; `angle(pair)` computes the angle (two-argument arctangent) of a vector. Use them to set endpoint directions and to compute bisectors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine dir and angle to make directional constructions (e.g., bisectors), set path endpoint directions with syntax p0{dir(30)}..p1, or use dir(-45) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrow drawing and customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `drawarrow` to draw a path with an arrowhead; `drawdblarrow` for double-headed arrows. Control arrowhead size with `ahlength` (default 4bp) and tip angle with `ahangle` (default 45 degrees). You can redefine the arrowhead procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust `ahlength`/`ahangle` or provide a custom `vardef arrowhead(expr p)` to change arrow appearance. Use `reverse()` for direction adjustments and `&` for joining path pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Built-in shapes and transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: MetaPost provides predefined paths such as fullcircle, halfcircle, quartercircle, unitsquare. Construct circles/ellipses/squares by scaling, rotating, and shifting these objects using `scaled`, `xscaled`, `yscaled`, `rotated`, `shifted`. Ordering of operators strongly influences final shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose transformations in the intended order (e.g., rotate then shift vs shift then rotate) and test visually; use units (u) for consistent sizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text labels and positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `label.suffix(string expression, pair)` and `dotlabel.suffix` with suffixes top, lft, rt, bot, ulft, urt, lrt, llft to position text relative to a pair. `labeloffset` sets distance from point to label. `defaultfont` and `defaultscale` control font selection and size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust `labeloffset` to avoid collisions. Use `btex ... etex` to typeset complex labels with TeX (generates .mpx). Use `verbatimtex ... etex` to set LaTeX preamble; avoid display math `$$...$$` inside btex—use \displaystyle instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using TeX for labels (btex/etex) and picture expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Between `btex` and `etex` you may pass typesetting commands to TeX; METAPOST suspends processing, TeX typesets and dvitomp translates the output into a picture expression (written to .mpx) that can be transformed and used in labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TeX for high-quality mathematical labels; the resulting picture expression can be scaled/rotated. Ensure proper preamble via `verbatimtex` if LaTeX is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: For-loops and repetition constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `for counter = start step stepsize until finish : ... endfor;` (or `for i=0 upto n:`) to repeat statements or to build up a single statement (e.g., constructing a path piecewise). `downto` is step -1 until.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loops can be used both to perform repeated drawing statements and to concatenate path segments (useful in plotting). Use `upto` for step 1 loops for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building graphs and function plotting idioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Define functions via `vardef f(expr x) = ... enddef;` and build paths for graphs with loops that append `.. (x,y)`. Use helper routines like compute_curve to assemble a path from sampled points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale x/y with ux/uy unit pairs; set xinc for resolution. For functions not built-in, implement via `mexp`/`mlog` scaled by 256 (see guidance on mexp/mlog).

rubrics_metrics.name: mexp/mlog scaling and custom math helpers
rubrics_metrics.description: METAPOST has built-in primitives mexp(x) = exp(x/256) and mlog(x) = 256 ln x. To define normal exp/ln/log functions, define wrapper vardefs scaling accordingly (e.g., vardef exp(expr x) = (mexp(256)**x) enddef;).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrap built-ins to expose convenient math APIs; reserve `log` for base-10 if desired by defining it explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive error handling and debugging
rubrics_metrics.description: If a processing error occurs METAPOST interrupts and shows an interactive prompt with options: press <return> to proceed, S to scroll, R to run without stopping, Q to run quietly, I to insert, E to edit file, numbers to ignore tokens, H for help, X to quit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press `e` to open the default editor at the spotted location (EDITOR or MPEDIT can be set); correct the source and re-run. METAPOST reports a line number where it spotted an issue but the actual error may be elsewhere—inspect surrounding code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pen specification and pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `draw path withpen pen_expression;` for temporary pen changes, and `pickup pen_expression;` to change the pen for subsequent draw statements. Default pen is circular with diameter 0.5 bp. `pencircle scaled numeric` sets pen width; create custom pens via `makepen(path)`. Pens can be transformed with xscaled/yscaled/rotated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use `pickup pencircle scaled N` for line thickness; transform pencircle for elliptical/calligraphic effects; create shape pens to draw custom markers (e.g., triangular markers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global drawing options with drawoptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The `drawoptions` function allows changing default settings for drawing operations (e.g., `drawoptions(dashed evenly withcolor red);`). `drawoptions()` resets defaults. beginfig automatically resets draw options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set global drawing style at figure start for consistent look; override per-draw when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashing and dash patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `draw path dashed dashpattern;`. `dashpattern` takes on/off distances (e.g., `dashpattern(on 6bp off 2bp on 2bp off 2bp)`). Predefined patterns include `evenly` and `withdots`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale dash patterns with `scaled` and shift start with `shifted` to align dashed patterns. Use helper macros to reuse patterns across drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour model and shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Color is an (r,g,b) triple with components in [0,1]. Predefined colors (red, green, blue, white, black) are available. Shades of gray: multiply `white` by scalar between 0 and 1. Use `withcolor` to set drawing/fill color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For grayscale conversion and perceptual adjustments, compare linear averaging `(r+g+b)/3` vs TV-weighted `0.30r + 0.59g + 0.11b`. Use color triples for precise color control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macros, vardef, scoping, and local variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Define reusable code with `def` and `vardef`. Use grouping and `save`/`begingroup` to create local variables and avoid global side-effects. Recursion is permitted in vardefs. Precedence rules of binary operators should be respected when writing expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use macros to encapsulate repeated drawing patterns (e.g., drawpoint, tick). Use `begingroup`/`endgroup` and `save` to localize names. Document macro arguments and side-effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using macro packages and inputting libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `input <package>;` to include macros (examples: courbes, grille, mpcirc). Packages provide higher-level routines for plots, circuits, vector fields, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review package documentation for turtle- vs node-based styles (e.g., mpcirc turtle-based by default). Prepare elements with package-specific calls (e.g., prepare(...) and edraw for mpcirc).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot annotation: ticks, labels and axes
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw tick marks and labels by computing tick coordinates (e.g., draw (i,-0.05)*ux--(i,0.05)*ux; label.bot(decimal(i), (i,0)*ux);). Use `labeloffset` for spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use loops to generate ticks/labels; use decimal() to convert numbers to strings for labeling; adjust `labeloffset` and `defaultscale` to control appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path interrogation utilities (point, direction, arctime, precontrol/postcontrol)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use `point i of path`, `direction t of path`, `arctime m of path` and `precontrol/postcontrol i of path` to inspect and use path geometry for advanced drawings (marking control points, drawing ticks, marking angles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these utilities when constructing proofs/illustrations that require access to local path geometry (e.g., marking equal lengths, drawing orthogonal ticks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking angles and lengths (geometric annotation macros)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement macros such as `tick`, `mark_angle`, and `mark_right_angle` to annotate equal segments and equal/right angles; use `turningnumber` to determine orientation (1 CCW, -1 CW) to make macros order-independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set user-adjustable constants (angle_radius, angle_delta, mark_size) to control annotation sizes; use unitvector and rotated directions to draw arcs/ticks robustly regardless of point ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector fields and directional fields visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute normalized direction vectors (e.g., unitvector((1,f(x,y))) scaled s) and draw small segments or arrows per grid point to illustrate directional/vector fields; draw solution curves superposed in different color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose grid spacing and scaling (u) for clarity; use different colors for vector field and solution curve; use package routines (e.g., courbes) when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riemann sum and area shading idiom
rubrics_metrics.description: Use loops to assemble and fill rectangular patches for Riemann sums: compute aa, bb, ff for each subinterval, form path cc := rpoint(aa,0)--rpoint(aa,ff)--rpoint(bb,ff)--rpoint(bb,0) and fill/draw with color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameterize a,b,n,h so minimal code changes adjust domain/partition; use `fill ... withcolor` to shade areas and `trace.courbe`/ftrace for curve outlines when using courbes package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated functions, cobweb and bifurcation plotting patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Use iterative loops to compute orbits and draw 'hooks' for cobweb plots or sample many parameter values and plot iterative values (e.g., logistic map bifurcation diagram) by plotting points (r*ux, x*uy) with small pen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run initial iterations to let transients die out, then plot subsequent iterates; choose pencircle scaled small for dense plots; loop over parameter r with sufficient resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface plotting & shading via finite-difference normals
rubrics_metrics.description: To produce shaded surface patches, sample surface z=f(x,y) on a grid, project 3D points to 2D via basis vectors, compute brightness factor with numerical derivatives (central differences), and fill each grid quad with color scaled by brightness factor * base_color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define project and brightnessfactor helper vardefs (diffx/diffy etc.), choose a light source location xp,yp,zp and bf (brightness factor). Use sufficiently fine nx,ny for smooth appearance but balance performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformations ordering matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying transformations (scaled, rotated, shifted, xscaled, yscaled) in different orders yields different final shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully order transformations and test; when composing many transforms, reason about coordinate frames (scale then rotate vs rotate then scale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding common pitfalls in TeX/MetaPost integration
rubrics_metrics.description: When using btex/etex with TeX or LaTeX preamble via verbatimtex, avoid display math `$$...$$` inside btex; prefer `\displaystyle ...` inside inline math to get displayed math style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set `verbatimtex` with %&latex and documentclass to ensure expected fonts/packages are available for typesetting labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactical approach: learn by examples and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning is best done from examples; exercises are provided to practice METAPOST rather than only reading about it. Compare answers with 'Solutions to the Exercises'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the step-by-step examples, type them yourself, experiment with parameter changes, and use provided exercises to build familiarity.
